findings.location: Proof, step 1.1 (time-reversal reduction); repeated in Remarks
findings.evidence: Step 1.1 says replacing N by -N preserves every development hypothesis and the fixed matter model. The admitted perfect-fluid and dust suppliers define future unit velocity fields n or u by g(n,N)<0 or g(u,N)<0 (def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model, clause (a); def-gr-dust-matter-model, clause (a)). Keeping those fields fixed while replacing N reverses the required sign, so the transformed tuples are not developments of those sectors. The general admissibility clauses do not require additional fixed models to be time-reversal covariant. Thus the reduction from a past-only corresponding-boundary set to the future-only exposure/restart suppliers is unjustified for the full stated scope. A past-directed exposure and restart proof preserving the fixed time orientation and fields, or an explicit verified time-reversal hypothesis and field transformation for the model class, is needed.
